pet-ex-pes-philadelphia-2019.n: Philadelphia Energy Solutions (PES) refinery fire and explosions
pet-ex-pes-philadelphia-2019.cp: incident-level (NOAA IncidentNews; precision varies, often approximate)
pet-ex-pes-philadelphia-2019.st: NOAA IncidentNews incident 9917 ('Philadelphia Energy Solutions Refinery Fires and Explosions; 3100 Passyunk Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19153, USA') point
pet-ex-pes-philadelphia-2019.what: CSB: about 4 a.m. on 21 June 2019 a vapor release in the PES alkylation unit found an ignition source, causing a fire and multiple explosions; CSB final report released 11 Oct 2022 with recommendations on hydrofluoric-acid alkylation safety.

src.t: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB), investigation page: PES Refinery Fire and Explosions
NOAA IncidentNews incident 9917: Philadelphia Energy Solutions Refinery Fires and Explosions; 3100 Passyunk Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19153, USA

pet-ex-bp-texas-city-2005.what: CSB: a series of explosions occurred while restarting a hydrocarbon isomerization unit; 15 workers were killed and 180 injured, many in or near work trailers by an atmospheric vent stack, after a distillation tower flooded with hydrocarbons and was overpressurized. The site is now the Galveston Bay Refinery.

src.t: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB), investigation page: BP America (Texas City) Refinery Explosion
EPA FRS facility 110059763536: GALVESTON BAY REFINERY, 2401 Fifth Avenue South, Texas City

pet-ex-itc-deer-park-2019.what: CSB: 'a massive tank fire erupted' at ITC Deer Park on 17 March 2019; final report released 6 Jul 2023. NOAA: the first tank on fire held 80,000 gallons of naphtha, with xylene and gas-blend tanks at risk.

src.t: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB), investigation page: Intercontinental Terminals Company (ITC) Tank Fire

pet-ex-capeco-bayamon-2009.what: CSB: a massive fire and explosion at the CAPECO terminal in Bayamón on 23 Oct 2009; the final report (21 Oct 2015) found inadequate management of the gasoline storage tank overfill hazard. NOAA: tanks with gasoline and diesel were on fire.

NOAA IncidentNews incident 8133: Caribbean Petroleum Corporation (CAPECO); San Juan, Puerto Rico

pet-ex-husky-superior-2018.what: CSB: the refinery was shutting down for a five-week turnaround when an explosion occurred, sending several people to hospitals; the final report (Dec 2022) covers a brittle fracture and asphalt fire. NOAA modeled the smoke plume.

NOAA IncidentNews incident 9711: Superior Refining Company Explosion Superior, WI; 2425 24th Ave E, Superior, WI 54880, USA

pet-ex-tesoro-anacortes-2010.what: CSB: a nearly forty-year-old heat exchanger catastrophically failed during maintenance, fatally injuring seven employees; cause was High Temperature Hydrogen Attack. CSB final report approved 1 May 2014.

EPA FRS facility 110020506460: CHEVRON REFINERY RICHMOND, 841 Chevron Way

pet-ex-deepwater-horizon-2010.st: NOAA IncidentNews incident 8220 ('Deepwater Horizon; Gulf of Mexico') point
pet-ex-deepwater-horizon-2010.what: CSB: a sudden explosion and fire on the rig killed 11 workers and started a massive spill; the rig was about 50 miles southeast of Venice, Louisiana, with 126 crew aboard. Volumes are in the spill record.

src.t: U.S. Chemical Safety Board (CSB), investigation page: Macondo Blowout and Explosion
NOAA IncidentNews incident 8220: Deepwater Horizon; Gulf of Mexico

pet-ex-bellingham-1999.n: Olympic Pipe Line gasoline rupture and fire, Whatcom Creek, Bellingham
pet-ex-bellingham-1999.st: List-only: NTSB gives no coordinate; NOAA has no incident record.
pet-ex-bellingham-1999.what: NTSB: the pipeline ruptured and released about 237,000 gallons of gasoline into a creek through Whatcom Falls Park; it ignited about 1.5 hours later and burned about 1.5 miles along the creek. Two 10-year-old boys and an 18-year-old died; eight more injuries.

src.t: NTSB Pipeline Accident Report PAR-02/02, Pipeline Rupture and Subsequent Fire in Bellingham, Washington, June 10, 1999

pet-ex-lac-megantic-2013.n: Lac-Mégantic crude-oil train derailment, explosions and fire
pet-ex-lac-megantic-2013.ty: Rail tank cars (unattended runaway train MMA-002)
pet-ex-lac-megantic-2013.st: List-only: TSB gives railway Mile 0.23, Sherbrooke Subdivision, not a coordinate.
pet-ex-lac-megantic-2013.what: TSB: 63 crude-oil tank cars and 2 box cars derailed in the town centre; about 6 million litres spilled and ignited, destroying 40 buildings and 53 vehicles; 47 people died and about 2,000 were evacuated.

src.t: Transportation Safety Board of Canada, Railway Investigation Report R13D0054 (Lac-Mégantic)

pet-ex-piper-alpha-1988.n: Piper Alpha platform explosion and fire, North Sea
pet-ex-piper-alpha-1988.ty: Offshore oil and gas production platform
pet-ex-piper-alpha-1988.st: List-only: no official coordinate read; the installation no longer exists.
pet-ex-piper-alpha-1988.what: Cullen inquiry: an initial explosion in the gas compression module set off escalating fires that destroyed the installation; 167 men died. The report made 106 recommendations, all accepted, leading to the offshore safety-case regime under HSE.

src.t: HSE, The Public Inquiry into the Piper Alpha Disaster (Cullen Report, Cm 1310, Nov 1990), vols 1-2
Hansard (UK Parliament), HC Deb 12 November 1990 vol 180 cc329-44, statement on the Piper Alpha inquiry report

pet-ex-buncefield-2005.n: Buncefield Oil Storage Depot explosion and fire, Hemel Hempstead
pet-ex-buncefield-2005.what: MIIB final report: a massive explosion followed by a fire that engulfed 23 large fuel storage tanks; 43 people suffered minor injuries and no one was killed. HSE's page says 'over 40 people were injured'.

src.t: Buncefield Major Incident Investigation Board, The Buncefield Incident 11 December 2005: Final Report, Volume 1 (2008) (official report; copy hosted by IChemE)
HSE, Response to the Buncefield incident (COMAH)

pet-ex-milford-haven-1994.n: Texaco Pembroke refinery explosion and fires, Milford Haven
pet-ex-milford-haven-1994.what: HSE: a severe electrical storm caused plant upsets; a control valve was shut while the control system showed it open, leading to an explosion and fires that burned until the evening of 26 July 1994.

src.t: HSE, COMAH case study: explosion and fires at the Texaco Refinery, Milford Haven, 24 July 1994 (summarizing the HSE investigation report)

pet-ex-feyzin-1966.what: ARIA No. 1: a badly conducted sampling drain on a propane sphere released LPG that ignited; the sphere exploded (BLEVE) and a neighboring sphere exploded at 9:40. 18 dead including 11 firefighters; 84 injured of 158 people present. HSE: five spheres destroyed.

src.t: BARPI (French Ministry of Ecological Transition), ARIA database accident No. 1, 'Catastrophe de Feyzin', 04/01/1966
HSE, COMAH case study: Refinery fire at Feyzin, 4th January 1966

pet-ex-amuay-2012.what: A Venezuelan government statement filed with the U.S. Justice Department under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (Aug 2025) says the explosion at Amuay, part of the Paraguaná Refining Complex, left 42 dead, 150 injured and heavy material damage. Contemporary injury counts varied.

src.t: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela informational material filed under FARA (registration 7023), 'Tragedia de Amuay' statement, 29 Aug 2025

pet-ex-jesse-1998.what: Pipeline fire at Jesse while residents collected leaking fuel. Death tolls of about 1,000 (1,082 is often called the official figure) appear only in secondary sources.
fig: about 1,000 (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

src.t: IFRC, Nigeria: Pipeline Explosion Information Bulletin No. 1 (21 Oct 1998) (page could not be opened)

pet-ex-san-juanico-1984.n: PEMEX LPG terminal explosions, San Juan Ixhuatepec (San Juanico)
pet-ex-san-juanico-1984.what: A series of LPG explosions at the PEMEX terminal destroyed much of the surrounding neighbourhood. The official toll, often cited as 503, was not read in an official document.
fig: about 500 (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

src.t: CENAPRED, Impacto socioeconómico de los principales desastres ocurridos en México 1980-1999

pet-ex-guadalajara-1992.ty: Municipal sewer (gasoline from a PEMEX pipeline)
pet-ex-guadalajara-1992.what: CEDHJ, citing official figures: explosions killed 212 people, left 69 missing, destroyed 8 km of streets and damaged 1,142 homes, 450 businesses, 100 schools and 600 vehicles.

src.t: Comisión Estatal de Derechos Humanos Jalisco, Pronunciamiento 1/2022 (22 de abril de 1992), citing official figures
CENAPRED, Impacto socioeconómico de los principales desastres ocurridos en México 1980-1999

pet-ex-tlahuelilpan-2019.what: Gasoline from an illegal tap on the PEMEX pipeline ignited while crowds collected fuel. Reported: health ministry counts rose from 114 (26 Jan 2019) to a final count of 137 in a Chamber of Deputies document, which could not be opened.
fig: 137 (final count; reported; not confirmed in an official source)

src.t: Secretaría de Gobernación SIL / Cámara de Diputados, document asun_3986718 (8 Jan 2020) on the Tlahuelilpan explosion (page could not be opened; text seen via search summary only)

pet-ex-matanzas-2022.what: Granma: on the evening of 5 Aug 2022 tank 52 was hit by lightning, starting a fire of serious proportions that spread to other tanks. The MINSAP toll of 16 dead and the loss of four of eight tanks were not read in an official page.
fig: 16 (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

src.t: Granma (official organ of the Communist Party of Cuba), 'Another tense day fighting fire at Matanzas Supertanker Depot' (9 Aug 2022)

pet-ex-qingdao-2013.n: Sinopec Donghuang crude pipeline leak and explosion, Qingdao
pet-ex-qingdao-2013.ty: Crude-oil pipeline leaking into a covered municipal drain
pet-ex-qingdao-2013.what: State Council investigation report (MEM): at 10:25 on 22 Nov 2013 crude from the Sinopec Donghuang pipeline entered a covered municipal drain in the Qingdao Economic and Technological Development Zone; vapor built up in the enclosed drain and exploded on sparks, killing 62 and injuring 136; direct losses 751.72 million yuan.

src.t: PRC Ministry of Emergency Management, State Council investigation report on the Qingdao '11·22' Sinopec Donghuang pipeline leak and explosion (Jan 2014)

pet-ex-jaipur-2009.n: Indian Oil Corporation Jaipur (Sitapura) terminal fire
pet-ex-jaipur-2009.what: A petrol leak during a transfer formed a vapour cloud that exploded, and the terminal burned for days. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas set up the M.B. Lal committee; its report was not read.
fig: 11 (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

src.t: Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (site could not be reached)

pet-ex-vila-soco-1984.n: Vila Socó gasoline pipeline fire, Cubatão
pet-ex-vila-soco-1984.ty: Petrobras gasoline pipeline under a stilt-house community
pet-ex-vila-soco-1984.what: Cubatão city government: officially 93 people died in the fire; the OAB Cubatão Truth Commission (since 2014) is examining whether the real number was higher.

src.t: Prefeitura de Cubatão, 'Vila Socó 40 anos – Cerimônias homenageiam vítimas do incêndio' (Feb 2024)

pet-ex-kuwait-oil-fires-1991.n: Kuwait oil well fires and blowouts (1991 Gulf War)
pet-ex-kuwait-oil-fires-1991.st: List-only: country-wide event; no single official point.
pet-ex-kuwait-oil-fires-1991.what: NOAA: many Kuwaiti oil wells were destroyed and set on fire, releasing far more oil and combustion products to land, air and water than the marine spill. UNCC: 163 wellhead pits from blown-out wells on land and 271.5 km² of tarcrete. See the oil-lakes record.

src.t: United Nations Compensation Commission, Follow-up Programme for Environmental Awards: State of Kuwait
NOAA IncidentNews incident 6786: Arabian Gulf Spills; Persian Gulf, Kuwait

pet-ex-qayyarah-2016.ty: Oil wells (set on fire by ISIL)
pet-ex-qayyarah-2016.what: UNEP: nineteen oil wells were set ablaze near Al Qayyarah, south-east of Mosul, as a scorched-earth tactic; the Directorate of Health with WHO treated over 1,000 suffocation cases in Qayyarah, Ijhala and Makhmour.

src.t: UN Environment Programme press release, 'Mosul battle brings environmental damage, with serious impacts on health, prospects of recovery' (2016)

pet-sp-exxon-valdez-1989.n: T/V Exxon Valdez grounding, Bligh Reef

pet-sp-exxon-valdez-1989.st: NOAA IncidentNews incident 6683 ('T/V Exxon Valdez; Bligh Reef, Prince William Sound, Alaska') point
pet-sp-exxon-valdez-1989.what: NOAA: ran aground on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound; spilled about 10.9 million of its 53 million gallons within six hours; oil reached over 1,100 miles of non-continuous Alaska coastline.
fig: about 10.9 million gallons (NOAA); about 11 million gallons (EVOSTC)

src.t: NOAA ORR, Exxon Valdez Oil Spill (significant incidents page)
Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council, Oil Spill Facts
NOAA IncidentNews incident 6683: T/V Exxon Valdez; Bligh Reef, Prince William Sound, Alaska

pet-sp-deepwater-horizon-2010.what: NOAA ORR: about 134 million gallons spilled before the well was capped three months later, the largest offshore spill in U.S. history. Judge Barbier's Phase Two findings: 4 million barrels left the reservoir, 3.19 million into the Gulf.
fig: 3.19 million barrels (about 134 million gallons) to the Gulf (E.D. La. Phase Two findings, 15 Jan 2015)

src.t: NOAA ORR, Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill (significant incidents page)

pet-sp-ixtoc-1979.what: NOAA: blew out in about 50 m of water after loss of drilling-mud circulation; oil and gas ignited and the platform collapsed into the wellhead area; two relief wells were drilled and the well was capped on 23 Mar 1980.

pet-sp-gulf-war-1991.what: NOAA: tankers and oil terminals in Kuwait were destroyed, releasing an estimated 6-8 million barrels into the Gulf. UNCC: over 800 miles of coastal area contaminated with oil.

src.t: United Nations Compensation Commission, Follow-up Programme for Environmental Awards: State of Kuwait
NOAA IncidentNews incident 6786: Arabian Gulf Spills; Persian Gulf, Kuwait

pet-sp-amoco-cadiz-1978.what: NOAA: steering failure; ran aground on Portsall Rocks three miles off Brittany; the entire cargo spilled; slick 18 by 80 miles; about 200 miles of coast and beaches of 76 Breton communities oiled.

src.t: NOAA IncidentNews incident 6241: Amoco Cadiz; Brittany, France

pet-sp-prestige-2002.n: T/V Prestige breakup and sinking off Galicia

pet-sp-prestige-2002.what: NOAA: in distress about 30 miles off Galicia on 13 Nov, towed offshore, sank on 19 Nov about 133 miles off the coast in almost 12,000 ft of water; oil kept leaking until cracks were sealed and the oil removed.

pet-sp-haven-1991.st: NOAA IncidentNews incident 6801 ('T/V Haven; Genoa, Italy') point

pet-sp-mayflower-2013.st: List-only: no NOAA or other official point found.
pet-sp-mayflower-2013.what: PHMSA Final Order: the Pegasus Pipeline failed in its Conway-Corsicana segment near Mayflower, releasing about 5,000 barrels of crude oil in a residential area.

pet-sp-keystone-mp14-2022.n: Keystone (Cushing Extension) rupture at Milepost 14, Mill Creek
pet-sp-keystone-mp14-2022.st: Blanked: NOAA approximate point in the wrong county.
pet-sp-keystone-mp14-2022.what: PHMSA: the 36-inch Keystone Cushing Extension ruptured in Washington County, Kansas at 9:01 p.m. CST; most of the oil flowed into Mill Creek; the cause was external loading on a 2010 replacement girth weld (inadequate backfill compaction). Reported: an estimated 12,937 barrels were released (the report PDF could not be opened at this check; figures read from its executive summary via a search summary).

pet-sp-montara-2009.n: Montara wellhead platform blowout, Timor Sea
pet-sp-montara-2009.st: List-only: the official 'Map of the location of the Montara Wellhead Platform' could not be downloaded.
pet-sp-montara-2009.what: Australian government: the leak took place in the Timor Sea off northern Western Australia between 21 Aug and 3 Nov 2009 after a wellhead accident on a PTTEP Australasia platform; the Commission of Inquiry made 105 recommendations.

src.t: Australian Department of Industry, Science and Resources, Montara Commission of Inquiry (publication page; report June 2010)

pet-sp-usinsk-1994.ty: Leaking crude-oil pipeline; failed containment dikes
pet-sp-usinsk-1994.what: World Bank: leaks from the Kharyaga-Usinsk pipeline caused one of the world's largest oil spills; in autumn 1994 over 20,000 tons (140,000 barrels) entered the Kolva River when temporary dikes failed in heavy rains.
fig: in excess of 100,000 tons (730,000 barrels) trapped in bogs and creeks; over 20,000 tons to the Kolva River (World Bank)

src.t: World Bank, Komi Emergency Oil Spill Recovery and Mitigation Project, project document (text)

pet-sp-norilsk-tpp3-2020.what: Reported: the Krasnoyarsk Arbitration Court (5 Feb 2021) ordered NTEK, a Nornickel subsidiary, to pay 146.177 billion rubles for environmental damage on Rosprirodnadzor’s claim (seen only in search summaries).
fig: about 21,000 tonnes (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

fig: about 723 barrels of oil and 2,620 barrels of oil-based mud (reported; not confirmed in an official source)

pet-co-greenpoint-1978.n: Greenpoint oil spill (former refineries and terminals), Newtown Creek, Brooklyn
pet-co-greenpoint-1978.ty: Free-product petroleum (oils, naphtha, kerosene, gasoline) on the water table; soil, groundwater and soil vapor
pet-co-greenpoint-1978.st: Active remediation under the 2010 federal consent decree
pet-co-greenpoint-1978.what: NYSDEC: a Coast Guard patrol saw oil entering Newtown Creek at Meeker Avenue on 2 Sept 1978; the spill area exceeded 52 acres and was estimated in 1979 at about 17 million gallons. NY Attorney General: the 2010 settlement (State of New York v. ExxonMobil, E.D.N.Y. 07-CV-2902) requires full cleanup and about $25 million in payments.

pet-co-red-hill-hawaii.n: Red Hill Bulk Fuel Storage Facility (Navy), Oahu
pet-co-red-hill-hawaii.ty: JP-5 jet fuel in the Red Hill Shaft drinking-water source and groundwater
pet-co-red-hill-hawaii.st: Closure and groundwater cleanup under the 2023 Consent Order
pet-co-red-hill-hawaii.dt: WWII-era tanks; 2021 releases; defueling and closure
pet-co-red-hill-hawaii.what: EPA: a May 2021 pressure surge released over 19,000 gallons of JP-5 that sat in a fire-suppression drain line until it ruptured on 20 Nov 2021, contaminating the Red Hill well; about 93,000 Navy water-system users were affected. DLNR: about 14,000 gallons of fuel is believed to have entered the Red Hill Shaft system.
fig: WWII-era tanks; 2021 releases; defueling and closure
over 19,000 gallons released 6 May 2021 (EPA); up to 19,377 gallons spilled 20 Nov 2021, up to 5,542 unrecovered (Navy)

pet-co-kirtland-bff.n: Kirtland AFB Bulk Fuels Facility jet-fuel plume, Albuquerque
pet-co-kirtland-bff.ty: Aviation gasoline, JP-4 and JP-8; ethylene dibromide (EDB) in the regional aquifer
pet-co-kirtland-bff.st: Active RCRA corrective action under NMED
pet-co-kirtland-bff.what: USAF (2011): between 1950 and 1999 a 16-inch underground offloading pipe leaked; pressure tests in Nov 1999 revealed the discharge; fuel reached groundwater about 500 ft down and migrated off base toward Albuquerque drinking-water wells. NMED oversees corrective action (2026 monitoring reports posted).
fig: 2 to 8 million gallons (USAF, 2011); reported later estimates up to 24 million gallons (ATSDR range 3 to 24 million; document could not be opened at this check)

pet-co-ogoniland-nigeria.dt: over 50 years of oil operations; assessed 2011
pet-co-ogoniland-nigeria.what: UNEP (2011): over 14 months the team examined more than 200 locations and 122 km of pipeline rights of way; at Nisisioken Ogale families drank well water with benzene over 900 times the WHO guideline, under an 8 cm layer of refined oil; recovery could take 25-30 years.
fig: over 50 years of oil operations; assessed 2011
